title: Stretch: Periodic vs Loose Sentences Adventure
welcome_lead: Stretch — analyse periodic and loose sentence structures used by master writers.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language stretch — periodic, loose, cumulative, balanced sentences and their effects.
final_note: You explored periodic, loose, cumulative and balanced sentences — and how each shapes the reader's experience.

concepts.def: Main clause delayed to the END for suspense
Loose sentence that piles up modifying detail
Flipping normal word order for effect

walkthroughs.body_html:
Periodic: 'After years of struggle, betrayal and quiet hope, she won.'

Main clause arrives LAST — pure suspense.

Loose: 'She won, after years of struggle, betrayal and quiet hope.'

Main idea first — clearer, more direct.

Balanced: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine.'

Inversion: 'Down came the rain' (not 'the rain came down') — Yoda-style emphasis.

mcqs.q: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine' is best described as:
options: Periodic
Loose
Balanced
Cumulative
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
The cooperative principle means people are always nice to each other.
The cooperative principle means everyone must agree in conversation.
The assumption that speakers cooperate in conversation by following maxims of quantity, quality, relation and manner — flouting these creates implicature.

mcqs.q: Why do text types have predictable features?
options: Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
Conventions develop because they serve communicative purpose — a recipe needs imperatives because it instructs; a news report needs the inverted pyramid because of how readers scan.
The cooperative principle means everyone must agree in conversation.
Text types have fixed features just because tradition says so.
